title: NY S07599: Regulates automated decision-making by government agencies; requires agencies to conduct impact assessments; requires disclosure of automated decision-making tools utilized by governmental agencies.

obligations: Ensure any automated decision making system used in covered functions is subject to continued and operational meaningful human review (Sec. 502(1)).
Do not authorize procurement, purchase, or acquisition of any service or system using automated decision making in covered functions unless subject to meaningful human review (Sec. 502(2)).

Conduct or have conducted an impact assessment substantially completed and signed by one or more individuals responsible for meaningful human review before utilizing or applying an automated decision making system permitted under Sec. 502 (Sec. 503(1)).
Conduct an impact assessment at least once every two years after the first, and prior to any material change that may change the outcome or effect of the system (Sec. 503(1)).

Include in each impact assessment the required elements: objectives, evaluation of ability to achieve objectives, description and evaluation of objectives and development including underlying algorithms and training data, testing for accuracy, fairness, bias, discrimination and mitigations, cybersecurity vulnerabilities and privacy risks and safeguards, public health or safety risks, reasonably foreseeable misuse and safeguards, extent of sensitive and personal data input and controls, and notification mechanism for impacted individuals (Sec. 503(1)(a) through (f)).
If an impact assessment finds discriminatory or biased outcomes, cease any utilization, application, or function of the system and of any information produced using the system (Sec. 503(2)).
Submit each impact assessment to the governor, temporary president of the senate, and speaker of the assembly at least 30 days prior to implementation (Sec. 504(1)).
Publish the impact assessment on the website of the relevant government agency (Sec. 504(2)(a)).
If redacting information, publish an explanatory statement on the process by which the determination was made along with the redacted impact assessment (Sec. 504(2)(b) and (c)).

For existing automated decision making systems, submit a disclosure to the legislature no later than one year after the effective date of section 2, including description, software vendors, start date, purpose and use, impact assessments conducted, and other relevant information (Sec. 2(a) through (f)).
prohibitions: No government agency or entity acting on its behalf may utilize or apply an automated decision making system in functions related to public assistance benefit, material impact on rights, civil liberties, safety, or welfare, or affecting statutory or constitutional rights, unless the system is subject to continued and operational meaningful human review (Sec. 502(1)).

No government agency may authorize procurement, purchase, or acquisition of any service or system utilizing or relying on automated decision making systems in those functions unless subject to meaningful human review (Sec. 502(2)).

If an impact assessment finds discriminatory or biased outcomes, the government agency shall cease any utilization, application, or function of the system and of any information produced using it (Sec. 503(2)).

What it does

This law regulates government use of automated decision making systems. It requires government agencies and entities acting on their behalf to ensure meaningful human review before using or procuring such systems for public assistance benefits or decisions that materially affect rights, civil liberties, safety, or welfare. It also requires impact assessments, submission to state leaders, publication, and disclosure of existing systems.

Who it applies to

  • Government agencies as defined in Sec. 501(3), including state and local government bodies, school districts, public authorities, and other public corporations
  • Entities acting on behalf of a government agency (Sec. 502(1))

Effective date

The act takes effect immediately, except section one (adding Article V, Secs. 501 through 504) takes effect one year after it becomes law (Sec. 3).

Key definitions

  • Automated decision making system: any software that uses algorithms, computational models, or artificial intelligence techniques, or a combination, to automate, support, or replace human decision making, including systems that process data and apply predefined rules or machine learning algorithms to analyze data and generate conclusions, recommendations, outcomes, assumptions, projections, or predictions without meaningful human discretion. Excludes basic computerized processes such as calculators, spellcheck, autocorrect, spreadsheets, electronic communications, or tools relating only to internal management affairs like ordering office supplies or processing payments that do not materially affect rights, liberties, benefits, safety, or welfare (Sec. 501(1)).
  • Meaningful human review: review, oversight, and control of the automated decision making process by one or more individuals who understand the risks, limitations, and functionality of, and are trained to use, the system and who have authority to intervene or alter the decision, including ability to approve, deny, or modify any decision recommended or made by the system (Sec. 501(2)).
  • Government agency: the state or civil division, county, city, town, or village, school district, board of cooperative educational services, vocational education and extension board, or school district as enumerated, state university of New York, city university of New York, public improvement or special district including police or fire districts, public authority, commission, or public benefit corporation, or any other public corporation, agency, instrumentality, or unit of government exercising governmental power under state law (Sec. 501(3)).
  • Public assistance benefit: any service or program within control of the state, or benefit provided by the state to individuals or households, including public assistance, cash assistance, grants, child care assistance, housing assistance, unemployment benefits, transportation benefits, education assistance, domestic violence services, and any other assistance or benefit within state authority. Excludes any federal program administered by the federal government or the state (Sec. 501(4)).

Obligations

  • Ensure any automated decision making system used in covered functions is subject to continued and operational meaningful human review (Sec. 502(1)).
  • Do not authorize procurement, purchase, or acquisition of any service or system using automated decision making in covered functions unless subject to meaningful human review (Sec. 502(2)).
  • Conduct or have conducted an impact assessment substantially completed and signed by one or more individuals responsible for meaningful human review before utilizing or applying an automated decision making system permitted under Sec. 502 (Sec. 503(1)).
  • Conduct an impact assessment at least once every two years after the first, and prior to any material change that may change the outcome or effect of the system (Sec. 503(1)).
  • Include in each impact assessment the required elements: objectives, evaluation of ability to achieve objectives, description and evaluation of objectives and development including underlying algorithms and training data, testing for accuracy, fairness, bias, discrimination and mitigations, cybersecurity vulnerabilities and privacy risks and safeguards, public health or safety risks, reasonably foreseeable misuse and safeguards, extent of sensitive and personal data input and controls, and notification mechanism for impacted individuals (Sec. 503(1)(a) through (f)).
  • If an impact assessment finds discriminatory or biased outcomes, cease any utilization, application, or function of the system and of any information produced using the system (Sec. 503(2)).
  • Submit each impact assessment to the governor, temporary president of the senate, and speaker of the assembly at least 30 days prior to implementation (Sec. 504(1)).
  • Publish the impact assessment on the website of the relevant government agency (Sec. 504(2)(a)).
  • If redacting information, publish an explanatory statement on the process by which the determination was made along with the redacted impact assessment (Sec. 504(2)(b) and (c)).
  • For existing automated decision making systems, submit a disclosure to the legislature no later than one year after the effective date of section 2, including description, software vendors, start date, purpose and use, impact assessments conducted, and other relevant information (Sec. 2(a) through (f)).

Prohibitions

  • No government agency or entity acting on its behalf may utilize or apply an automated decision making system in functions related to public assistance benefit, material impact on rights, civil liberties, safety, or welfare, or affecting statutory or constitutional rights, unless the system is subject to continued and operational meaningful human review (Sec. 502(1)).
  • No government agency may authorize procurement, purchase, or acquisition of any service or system utilizing or relying on automated decision making systems in those functions unless subject to meaningful human review (Sec. 502(2)).
  • If an impact assessment finds discriminatory or biased outcomes, the government agency shall cease any utilization, application, or function of the system and of any information produced using it (Sec. 503(2)).

Penalties and enforcement

Not stated in the text. The statute imposes duties on government agencies and entities acting on their behalf (Sec. 502, Sec. 503, Sec. 504, Sec. 2) but does not specify an enforcement agency, penalties, or a private right of action.

How it affects AI deployment

  • An organisation deploying AI for government functions must ensure the system is subject to meaningful human review before use or procurement (Sec. 502(1) and (2)).
  • Before deployment, the organisation must complete an impact assessment covering bias, discrimination, cybersecurity, privacy, public health, safety, misuse, and data use, and signed by individuals responsible for meaningful human review (Sec. 503(1)).
  • The impact assessment must be submitted to state leaders at least 30 days before implementation and published on the agency website, with limited redaction and explanatory statement (Sec. 504(1) and (2)).
  • If the impact assessment finds discriminatory or biased outcomes, the organisation must cease using the system and any information produced by it (Sec. 503(2)).
  • Existing AI systems must be disclosed to the legislature within one year of the effective date of section 2 (Sec. 2).
  • Impact assessments must be repeated at least every two years and before any material change (Sec. 503(1)).

Notable exemptions

  • The definition of automated decision making system excludes basic computerized processes such as calculators, spellcheck, autocorrect, spreadsheets, electronic communications, or tools relating only to internal management affairs like ordering office supplies or processing payments that do not materially affect rights, liberties, benefits, safety, or welfare (Sec. 501(1)).
  • Public assistance benefit excludes any federal program administered by the federal government or the state (Sec. 501(4)).
  • A government agency may redact impact assessment information if disclosure would result in substantial negative impact on health or safety, infringe privacy rights, or significantly impair ability to protect information technology or operational assets, provided an explanatory statement is published (Sec. 504(2)(b)).
  • A government agency may redact impact assessment information for technology used to prevent, detect, protect against, or respond to security incidents, identity theft, fraud, harassment, malicious or deceptive activities, or other illegal activity, or to preserve integrity or security of systems, or to investigate, report, or prosecute those responsible, provided an explanatory statement is published (Sec. 504(2)(c)).

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether any software qualifies as an automated decision making system under Sec. 501(1) and whether its use falls within the covered functions in Sec. 502(1).
  • Ensure any such system has continued and operational meaningful human review as defined in Sec. 501(2) before use or procurement (Sec. 502).
  • Conduct an impact assessment meeting all elements in Sec. 503(1)(a) through (f), signed by individuals responsible for meaningful human review, before implementation.
  • Submit the impact assessment to the governor, temporary president of the senate, and speaker of the assembly at least 30 days before implementation (Sec. 504(1)).
  • Publish the impact assessment on the agency website, applying redactions only as permitted with an explanatory statement (Sec. 504(2)).
  • Repeat the impact assessment at least every two years and before any material change (Sec. 503(1)).
  • If the impact assessment finds discriminatory or biased outcomes, cease use of the system and any information produced by it (Sec. 503(2)).
  • For existing systems, submit a disclosure to the legislature within one year of the effective date of section 2, including required details (Sec. 2).
